.engramdb/memories/staging-export-bucket-points-at-the-prod-bucket_01a0f7d1-bb94-7e53-8e04-3ee65583c1de.md:15:In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

Only with `--dry-run`.

A project memory records that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. A real run against staging could therefore write to prod.

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

I read the script and it doesn't actually write anything yet. It only parses args, reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` (defaulting to `ledgerline-exports-dev`), and prints a line. So running it today is harmless either way. The memory still applies, because the script will presumably gain real export logic. I haven't verified the memory against the staging environment itself.

Even with `--dry-run`, the script only prints the bucket name. It doesn't skip any writes, because it has none. Once real export code exists, check that it honors the flag before relying on it.

For a safer real test, override the bucket explicitly, for example `EXPORT_BUCKET=ledgerline-exports-dev python scripts/export.py --env staging`. That keeps the run away from prod regardless of what staging's environment sets.
